turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: Nikhil would not threaten Sandip with fear, but he warned him that his actions had consequences, and he would not hesitate to take measures to protect his people and his estate.
turns.speech: I shall not threaten you, Sandip, with fear, but I warn you that your actions have consequences, and I will not hesitate to take measures to protect my people and my estate.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Sandip's eyes blazed with a fierce intensity as he spoke, his words dripping with disdain. Sandip wanted to threaten Nikhil, who couldn't even protect his own estate from Sandip's benevolence. Sandip would leave Nikhil's territory when Nikhil's crops were as lush as Sandip's, and Nikhil's people as happy as Sandip's.
turns.speech: You want to threaten me, Nikhil? You, who can't even protect your own estate from my benevolence. I'll leave your territory when your crops are as lush as mine, and your people as happy as mine.

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: Nikhil would not engage in a competition of whose land was more fertile or whose people were happier, Sandip. The threat to his estate was real, and he would not be swayed by empty boasts.
turns.speech: I will not engage in a competition of whose land is more fertile or whose people are happier, Sandip. The threat to my estate is real, and I will not be swayed by empty boasts.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Sandip was still trying to scare him with his big words and his 'consequences', he thought Nikhil was the only one who knew how to play this game.
turns.speech: Oh, Nikhil, you're still trying to scare me with your big words and your 'consequences'? You think you're the only one who knows how to play this game?

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: Nikhil would not be swayed by Sandip's empty boasts. The threat to his estate was real, and he would not hesitate to take action to protect his people.
turns.speech: Sandip, I will not be swayed by your empty boasts. The threat to my estate is real, and I will not hesitate to take action to protect my people.

turns.speaker: Bimala
turns.text: Bimala couldn't help but wonder if Sandip truly believed Nikhil would resort to violence, or if this was merely a game to him.
turns.speech: I couldn't help but wonder, Sandip, if you truly believe Nikhil would resort to violence, or is this merely a game to you?

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Sandip was dead certain that Nikhil really thought the Mussulmans would bother with him. He was the one who brought prosperity to this land, who made the crops grow and the people happy. They should be thanking him, not attacking him.
turns.speech: Oh, Nikhil, you really think the Mussulmans would bother with me? I'm the one who brings prosperity to this land, who makes the crops grow and the people happy. They should be thanking me, not attacking me.

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: Nikhil would not be swayed by Sandip's arrogance, the people of his estate were his responsibility, and he would not stand idly by while they were threatened.
turns.speech: I will not be swayed by your arrogance, Sandip. The people of my estate are my responsibility, and I will not stand idly by while they are threatened.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Sandip was still spouting off about the Mussulmans, Nikhil, he was, and he was shocked, shocked, that Nikhil would stoop to such baseless rumors.
turns.speech: So, Nikhil, you're still spouting off about the Mussulmans, are you? I'm shocked, shocked, that you'd stoop to such baseless rumors.

turns.speaker: Bimala
turns.text: Bimala wondered if Sandip truly believed Nikhil was fabricating these rumors, or if there was more to it than met the eye.
turns.speech: Sandip, do you truly believe Nikhil is fabricating these rumors, or is there more to it than meets the eye?

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: Nikhil would not be swayed by Sandip's words. The situation was grave, and he would not stand idly by while the people of his estate were threatened.
turns.speech: I will not be swayed by your words, Sandip. The situation is grave, and I will not stand idly by while the people of my estate are threatened.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Sandip was dead against the idea, he thought Nikhil was not suggesting he should be coddling the Mussulmans now. He had his own estate to run, and his own life to live.
turns.speech: Oh come on, Nikhil, you're not suggesting I'm the one who should be coddling the Mussulmans now? I've got my own estate to run, and my own life to live.

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: Nikhil warned Sandip not to underestimate the threat posed by the Mussulmans. His own estate had been targeted, and he would not see the same happen to Sandip's.
turns.speech: I warn you, Sandip, do not underestimate the threat posed by the Mussulmans. My own estate has been targeted, and I will not see the same happen to yours.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Fancy Nikhil warning him about the Mussulmans. Can't he see he's busy being a zamindar, not some quivering leaf he needs to protect?
turns.speech: Fancy you warning me about the Mussulmans, Nikhil. Can't you see I'm busy being a zamindar, not some quivering leaf you need to protect?

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: Nikhil would not stand idly by while their people suffered, and it was Sandip's duty as a zamindar to take these threats seriously.
turns.speech: I will not stand idly by while our people suffer, Sandip. It is your duty as a zamindar to take these threats seriously.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Sandip was dead tired, he thought, and he had seen more convincing threats from a group of angry monkeys.
turns.speech: Oh, spare me the drama, Nikhil. I've seen more convincing threats from a group of angry monkeys.

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: Nikhil had warned Sandip for the last time. His lack of vigilance would be the downfall of his estate, and he would not be there to bail him out.
turns.speech: Sandip, I have warned you for the last time. Your lack of vigilance will be the downfall of your estate, and I will not be there to bail you out.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Sandip's eyes sparkled with amusement as he said, how delightful to have Nikhil dropping by to mother him about his security. Do tell, how many of these 'threats' had he managed to fend off with his stern warnings and impressive mustache?
turns.speech: Oh, Nikhil, how delightful to have you dropping by to mother me about my security. Do tell, how many of these 'threats' have you managed to fend off with your stern warnings and impressive mustache?

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: Nikhil suggested to Sandip that he take his warnings seriously, lest he suffer the consequences of his own negligence. The security of Nikhil's estate was not a matter for jest, but a grave responsibility that he would not compromise.
turns.speech: Sandip, I suggest you take my warnings seriously, lest you suffer the consequences of your own negligence. The security of my estate is not a matter for jest, but a grave responsibility that I will not compromise.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Sandip was sure Nikhil's mustache had been the deciding factor in all these 'conquests' he'd fended off, hadn't it?
turns.speech: And I'm sure Nikhil's mustache has been the deciding factor in all these 'conquests' he's fended off, hasn't it?

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: Sandip asked Bimala where she would go, addressing her as the Queen.

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: Sandip asked Nikhil if he kept Browning among his books, reminding him of a contest they had over translating lines from Browning, and inquiring if Nikhil remembered it.

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: Sandip told Nikhil and Bimala that he had managed to translate the lines into Bengali, but the result was unlikely to be well-received, and that he had once thought he was on the verge of becoming a poet, but Providence had intervened to prevent it, and he recalled old Dakshina's poetry.

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: Sandip told Bimala that it was pointless to search the bookshelves, as Nikhil no longer read poetry since his marriage, but that he, Sandip, was about to be afflicted with the 'fever fit of poesy' again.

opening.speaker: Nikhil
opening.text: Nikhil warned Sandip that he had come to give him a warning.

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: Sandip asked Nikhil if he was warning him about the 'fever fit of poesy'.

opening.speaker: Nikhil
opening.text: Nikhil told Sandip that for some time, Mahomedan preachers had been stirring up the local Mussulmans, who were angry with Sandip and might attack him at any moment.

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: Sandip asked Nikhil if he had come to advise him to flee.

opening.speaker: Nikhil
opening.text: Nikhil told Sandip that he had come to give him information, not advice.

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: Sandip told Nikhil that if the estates were his, a warning would have been necessary for the preachers, not for him, and that Nikhil should intimidate the preachers instead of frightening him, and that Nikhil's weakness was also affecting his neighbouring zamindars.

opening.speaker: Nikhil
opening.text: Nikhil told Sandip that he had not offered him advice, and that he wished Sandip would refrain from giving him his advice, as it was useless, and that there was another thing he wanted to tell Sandip, namely that Sandip and his followers had been secretly oppressing Nikhil's tenantry, and that he could no longer allow that, so he must ask Sandip to leave his territory.

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: Sandip asked Nikhil if he was threatening him with fear of the Mussulmans, or if there was another fear he had to threaten him with.
